title: The derived limit of the tower adjunction is an integral adjunction
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$ and its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaves, the derived-complete categories $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$, coefficient towers and normalized constructible towers [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Reductions are derived tensor products with $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$; integral pullback and twists mean [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Use the compact-support direct image of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] (with a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$) and the tower adjunction of [det-sp-tower-gluing].

For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the tower $f_\bullet^!\operatorname{red}_YK$ is normalized
constructible, so
$H_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)=R\varprojlim_nf^!_{\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(K/\ell^n)\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$
and $\operatorname{red}_XH_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)\simeq f_\bullet^!\operatorname{red}_YK$. For
$M\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ there are bijections, natural in $M$ and $K$,

$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}M,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rf_{!,\bullet}\operatorname{red}_XM,\operatorname{red}_YK)
\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{red}_XM,f_\bullet^!\operatorname{red}_YK)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,H_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)),
$$

so $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}\dashv H_{f,\mathcal O_E}$, with unit and counit the derived
limits of the tower unit and counit, whose reductions are the finite units and
counits. Moreover
$\gamma_{f,\mathcal O_E}^H(K)=R\varprojlim\gamma_{f,\bullet}(\operatorname{red}_YK):
f^*_{\mathcal O_E}K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
*Normalization.* $\operatorname{red}_YK$ is normalized constructible, and $f^!_\bullet$
preserves normalized constructible towers ([det-sp-tower-gamma], (3)). By the
equivalence of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], $H_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)=R\varprojlim
f^!_\bullet\operatorname{red}_YK$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and
$\operatorname{red}_XH_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K)\simeq f^!_\bullet\operatorname{red}_YK$ (counit isomorphism on
normalized towers). Functoriality of $H$ follows from that of $f^!_\bullet$.

Put $r_T=\operatorname{red}_T$, $L_T=R\varprojlim$, $F=Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}$, $F_\bullet=Rf_{!,\bullet}$ and $G_\bullet=f^!_\bullet$. Apply clause (2) of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] to $M$ and the chosen compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$. It identifies $FM$ with $L_YF_\bullet r_XM$ in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and supplies the canonical comparison $b_M:r_YFM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\bullet r_XM$. These reduction/reconstruction comparisons are functorial: for $a:M\to M'$, $F_\bullet r_X(a)\,b_M=b_{M'}\,r_YF(a)$, since both composites are induced by the same maps of reduced complexes. Step 1 gives a natural comparison $c_K:r_XH(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_\bullet r_YK$. Full faithfulness of $r_Y$ and $r_X$ from [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], followed by the tower adjunction of [det-sp-tower-gluing], gives exactly the three displayed bijections. Full faithfulness acts on a morphism by reduction; the first comparison sends $a:FM\to K$ to $r_Y(a)b_M^{-1}$, and the last sends $h:r_XM\to G_\bullet r_YK$ to the unique $\widetilde h:M\to H(K)$ with $r_X(\widetilde h)=c_K^{-1}h$. These operations are natural in both variables, hence their composite is an adjunction bijection.

Write $\eta^\bullet$ and $\varepsilon^\bullet$ for the tower unit and counit. The unit $\eta_M:M\to H(FM)$ is the image of $1_{FM}$ under this bijection and the counit $\varepsilon_K:FH(K)\to K$ is the inverse image of $1_{H(K)}$. Substitution in the preceding formulas gives
$$r_X(\eta_M)=c_{FM}^{-1}\,G_\bullet(b_M^{-1})\,\eta^\bullet_{r_XM},\qquad
r_Y(\varepsilon_K)=\varepsilon^\bullet_{r_YK}\,F_\bullet(c_K)\,b_{H(K)}.$$
Here composition is read right to left. The two triangle identities can be checked explicitly. Naturality of $b$ at $\eta_M$ and then naturality of the tower counit give
$$r_Y(\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M)=\varepsilon^\bullet_{r_YFM}\,F_\bullet G_\bullet(b_M^{-1})\,F_\bullet(\eta^\bullet_{r_XM})\,b_M=b_M^{-1}\,\varepsilon^\bullet_{F_\bullet r_XM}\,F_\bullet(\eta^\bullet_{r_XM})\,b_M=1.$$
Naturality of $c$ at $\varepsilon_K$ and then naturality of the tower unit give
$$r_X(H\varepsilon_K\circ\eta_{H(K)})=c_K^{-1}\,G_\bullet(\varepsilon^\bullet_{r_YK})\,G_\bullet F_\bullet(c_K)\,\eta^\bullet_{r_XH(K)}=c_K^{-1}\,G_\bullet(\varepsilon^\bullet_{r_YK})\,\eta^\bullet_{G_\bullet r_YK}\,c_K=1.$$
The last equalities are the two tower triangle identities. Faithfulness of $r_X,r_Y$ gives the integral identities. If $u_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Tr_TA$ is the reconstruction unit, each displayed reduced map $v:r_TA\to r_TB$ lifts as $u_B^{-1}L_T(v)u_A$, by naturality of $u$. Thus these unit and counit maps are precisely the derived limits of the tower maps under the displayed canonical identifications. Evaluating the formulas at level $n$ gives the finite units and counits, by clause (3) of [det-sp-tower-gluing].

Let $P=f^*_{\mathcal O_E}K(d)[2d]$. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], integral pullback preserves $\Dbc$ and its canonical reductions are $f^*_{\mathcal O_E/\ell^n}(K/\ell^n)$. The powers $(\ell^n)$ are a cofinal subsequence of the uniformizer powers: $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{en})$, where $e$ is the ramification index. The cited reduction formulas therefore apply at these levels. By [prop-weil-twist-preserves], the integral twist is an invertible locally free rank-one sheaf, preserves $\Dbc$, and has the finite twists as reductions. Locally trivializing this line identifies its tensor comparison with $N\otimes^L_{R_X}R_X\otimes^L_{R_X}B_n=N\otimes^L_{R_X}B_n$, where $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_X$; hence this comparison is an isomorphism. Shifts commute with reduction because shifting a complex commutes termwise with tensor and its differential. These canonical comparisons commute with quotient transitions (both composites multiply the coefficient factors), and give $r_XP\simeq f^*_\bullet r_YK(d)[2d]$. In particular $P\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is derived complete. Clause (2) of [det-sp-tower-gamma] now supplies a tower isomorphism $r_XP\xrightarrow{\sim}G_\bullet r_YK$. Apply the functor $L_X=R\varprojlim$ and precompose with the reconstruction unit $P\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Xr_XP$ of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. The composite is the stated $\gamma^H_{f,\mathcal O_E}(K):P\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K)$; a functor carries an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps.

statement_correction.what: The imported sentence has free f,d,E,ell,X and no geometric domain. For example, the map from a countable disjoint union of Spec k to Spec k is smooth separated of pure dimension zero but is not finite type, outside the named compact-support/exceptional interfaces. The correction spells out the separated finite-type geometric domain and the coefficient context already required by the chapter and the cited definitions; every displayed conclusion is retained.
